added_failures_note: measured from the reviewed run's own gate logs: baseline_suite at aefb607f7f records exit_status 1, completed true, failure_count 8 with 8 ids (base-arm.log, last line EXIT=1), and after_suite at a89931102c records exit_status 0, completed true, failure_count 0 (head-arm.log, last line EXIT=0), so the added set is empty; the eight base ids are the node's own arms failing before the feature existed.

findings.text: passed[plan_slug] = edited is recorded for every compose attempt regardless of result.get('dispatched'), so a plan whose review dispatch was refused (a budget-hold or lane-paused report from recovery_review_dispatch.dispatch_review_for_run that left no queued run) is stamped as weighed at its current mtime and never retried until the author edits the plan; before this commit every pass re-weighed it, and the plan's review is silently never composed, which is the deliverable the node exists to produce. No test covers a non-dispatched compose being retried.

PLAN_REVIEW_PASS_LIMIT=1 is checked before weighing and the loop restarts from the first plan each pass, so a plan near the head whose skip reason does not settle (the burst refusal from compose_burst_refusal at :2499, whose text starts 'unit ...' and matches neither settle prefix at :2599) holds the single read slot every pass and no later edited plan in the project is ever weighed until that plan's author answers its findings.

_plans_by_hand duplicates the resource catalogue's classification instead of using it: reckon/resources.py:313 _identify_resource owns the location-versus-declared-type rule and resource_scan_scope (:478) already yields the files a scan dropped, so iter_resources(..., ignore_invalid=True) plus that dropped record would answer the same question in one walk; the copy diverges by filtering only on an immediate parent directory and by applying no INFRA_DIRS or evidence-fragment rule (reckon/resources.py:379), so the fallback path can admit documents the catalogue deliberately excludes.
